newsitem.title: USA: Federal Signal backs '97 earnings estimates.
newsitem.headline: Federal Signal backs '97 earnings estimates.

text.p: Federal Signal Corp expects its 1997 profit to show a single-digit percentage increase and backs earnings estimates for the year in a range of $1.36 to $1.43 a share, the company's chief executive said Tuesday.
"We're as confident as we can be that the fourth quarter's going to improve very well," Joseph Ross told Reuters.

"We're comfortable with the range of First Call estimates for EPS for the year. Unfortunately, the most likely circumstance will be a year of single-digit growth in income," Ross said after a presentation at a Piper Jaffray investment conference in Minneapolis.
In 1996, the Oakbrook, Illinois-based diversified manufacturer earned $1.29 a share.
Last week, the company estimated its 1997 second and third quarter earnings would show no change from the year-earlier periods because of short-term order deferrals.
Ross said the company's vehicle group, which makes emergency vehicles and street sweepers, would probably not achieve double-digit operating margins in 1997.

"The main reason we've seen vehicle operating margins erode is because of the acquisitions we've done," Ross said. "While we have a couple of companies within vehicle operating at double-digit margins, I doubt we'll have double-digit margins for the vehicle group for the year."
In the 1997 first quarter, the vehicle group had an operating margin of 9.3 percent, up from 8.5 percent in 1996.

Ross said he expected "mid-single digit growth in the tool group's sales in 1997." The tool group makes special die components and precision parts for the automotive and appliance industries and grooving tool systems for the automotive and construction-equipment industries.
